subject: Clarify: Non-learning commitment, EU residency, and deletion/tombstone timeline
messages:
From: Elaine Miller <elaine.miller@stellarfinance.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@stellarfinance.com
Date: Wed, 1 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on 'not used for model training' + deletion timing

Hi Marissa,

Quick question as we finish procurement: can Redwood provide a written, contract‑grade statement that customer content will not be used to train models (for model updates or downstream training)? Stellar needs clear language for our legal/compliance team.

A few follow-ups we'd like clarified in a single doc or addendum:
- Exact scope of "not used for model training" (does it include telemetry, logs, debug snapshots, and ephemeral caches?)
- How retention and deletion requests are implemented: timeline from customer request to data no longer accessible, and when backups/snapshots are purged.
- Residency guarantees: if we select EU region, does all production and backup data remain in EU? Are there exceptions (support workflows, audit copies)?

Can you share any templates or evidence (SOC 2, artifact, or wording you recommend for the contract)? We have a target signing window next week.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Miller
VP, Product Risk & Compliance
Stellar Finance

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Miller <elaine.miller@stellarfinance.com>
Cc: procurement@stellarfinance.com
Date: Wed, 1 Oct 2025 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'not used for model training' + deletion timing

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide an addendum and supporting evidence. High level answers inline below; I can attach a short PDF summarizing this for signature and loop in our security/ops owners if you'd like more technical detail.

- "Not used for model training": Redwood offers a contractual non‑training commitment for paid customers. That commitment covers any textual payloads sent to the inference API, associated request metadata, and customer‑scoped telemetry used for billing. It excludes aggregated, anonymized operational metrics used to monitor our service (e.g., token rates, error rates) unless you opt into sharing. We do not incorporate customer payloads into model training pipelines.

- Retention/deletion timeline: upon a verified deletion request we mark customer records for deletion (tombstone) immediately; application‑level access stops within minutes. Production data is removed from live stores within 24–72 hours depending on region and job windows. Backups and snapshots are scheduled for purging within 90 days unless you choose a shorter contractual TTL; we can provide a 30‑day backup purge SLA in the contract for EU Dedicated/Private deployments.

- Residency: when you select EU residency, primary storage, inference compute, and backups are restricted to EU regions. Support engineers may run transient diagnostics using obfuscated data only with your approval. We provide customer‑managed encryption keys (KMS) for higher assurance.

I'll attach a short summary doc (redwood-nontrain-commitment.pdf) and propose an addendum clause you can share with legal. Would you like us to prepare a DocuSign addendum for signature?

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Oct 2025 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Question on 'not used for model training' + deletion timing

Marissa / Sean — drafting the appendix and a CSV retention outline attached. High‑level technical points you can include in the appendix:

1) Coverage of "non‑training"
- Customer payloads: payloads, prompt/response pairs, uploaded files, and user metadata are excluded from any training or fine‑tuning efforts performed by Redwood.
- Telemetry: operational metrics (error counts, latency histograms) are collected at aggregate levels and are not linkable back to customer payloads.
- Debug traces & snapshots: ephemeral debug traces (e.g., limited KV cache dumps used for reproducing an incident) are accessible only to authorized ops engineers and are redacted/obfuscated; they are not used for model training.

2) Deletion workflow and timelines
- Step 1 (T0): On verified deletion request we create a tombstone flag immediately; application reads treat the record as deleted.
- Step 2 (T0 + minutes→hours): Live storage removal — primary indexes and object pointers removed (target 24–72 hours window depending on sharded job schedules).
- Step 3 (T0 + up to 90 days): Backups & snapshots purge — standard schedule is 90 days for hosted; we support contractually reducing this to 30 days for EU Dedicated/Private customers.
- Step 4 (T0 + up to 180 days): Third‑party audit/archival exceptions — if you request explicit audit exports before purge we will retain only the exported artifact and apply redaction; otherwise no copies remain.

3) Backups/snapshots nuances
- Incremental backups retain only delta blocks; full data purge requires the retention window to lapse and background compaction to run. We guarantee deletion from snapshot index within the contracted window; actual physical block reclamation follows the cloud provider's compaction timeline (we track and can report progress).

4) Residency & support
- EU residency: primary compute, primary storage, and backups are provisioned in EU regions.
- Support access: support sessions that require data access are performed within EU compute when requested; by default support uses redacted artifacts.
- KMS: Customer‑managed KMS is available; revoking keys renders stored backups unreadable.

5) Evidence and artifacts
- We can provide a SOC 2 summary and a signed non‑training addendum. I attached a CSV schedule that maps hostnames/regions -> retention TTLs for typical deployments.

Attachments: data-retention-schedule.csv

If Marissa confirms, I'll convert this into a 1‑page technical appendix and Sean can add the commercial SLA options.

— Mina
Head of Platform Security (Ops)

Hi Elaine — thanks for the patience. Attaching the non‑training PDF and technical appendix we prepared. Summary below and next steps: 

Summary (contract language we propose):
"Redwood Inference warrants that Customer Data (defined as any payload or file transmitted by the Customer to the Redwood inference API) will not be used to train, fine‑tune, or improve Redwood models. Redwood may process aggregate, anonymized operational telemetry for service health and capacity planning, which does not contain Customer Data in identifiable form."

Deletion & retention bullets we will include in the addendum:
- Immediate tombstone on request; live access removed within 24–72 hours.
- Hosted backup/snapshot purge within 90 days by default; contractual option for 30‑day backup purge for EU Dedicated/Private.
- Customer‑managed KMS option: revocation makes any remaining encrypted snapshots unreadable.
- Support access to customer data is restricted and logged; support sessions that require access to unredacted data must be approved by the customer.

Evidence: SOC 2 summary attached and a DocuSign link to the addendum below. If you agree, Sean will prepare the final commercial term (30‑day backup SLA option) and route the addendum for signature.
